root_cause.text: In Landlock’s `hook_cred_transfer()` (`security/landlock/cred.c`), the per-credential security blob was only copied when `old_llcred->domain` was non-NULL, so `log_subdomains_off` set by `landlock_restrict_self(..., ruleset_fd = -1)` on a domain-less credential was lost during `fork()`/`prepare_creds()`.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description says `landlock_restrict_self()` can set `LOG_SUBDOMAINS_OFF` “without creating a domain” and that this “is committed but not preserved across fork() because the child's prepare_creds() calls hook_cred_transfer() which skips the copy when domain is NULL”; the patch removes the `if (old_llcred->domain)` guard and unconditionally copies `*landlock_cred(new) = *old_llcred;`, confirming the missing inheritance path.

intent_record.intent_summary: Always propagate Landlock credential state during credential transfer instead of skipping it when the old domain is absent.
intent_record.what: In `hook_cred_transfer()`, the conditional `if (old_llcred->domain) { ... }` was removed. The two statements inside it, `landlock_get_ruleset(old_llcred->domain);` and `*landlock_cred(new) = *old_llcred;`, are now always executed unconditionally.
intent_record.how: At runtime, credential transfer now always copies the old Landlock credential state into the new credential and always attempts to take a reference on `old_llcred->domain`, even when that domain pointer is NULL. This changes behavior from skipping Landlock state propagation for credentials without a domain to unconditionally propagating it, which may expose or fix missing credential state handling.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add coverage proving `log_subdomains_off` is inherited across fork even when set before domain creation, so subdomain audit logs are correctly suppressed in children.
intent_record.what: A new `TEST_F(audit, log_subdomains_off_fork)` test was added. It creates a Landlock ruleset with `LANDLOCK_SCOPE_SIGNAL`, forks once to verify a denial is logged before muting, then calls `landlock_restrict_self(-1, LANDLOCK_RESTRICT_SELF_LOG_SUBDOMAINS_OFF)` to enable subdomain log muting without creating a domain, forks again, and verifies the second child’s denial is not logged. The test also drains audit records between phases and closes the ruleset FD at the end.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the test checks that the `log_subdomains_off` state is preserved across `fork()` even when the parent has no Landlock domain yet. This ensures that a child creating a domain after inheriting that state will have logging disabled for subdomain events, preventing audit records for the second denial while still allowing the first denial to be logged as a baseline.

grouping_result.intent: Always propagate Landlock credential state during credential transfer instead of skipping it when the old domain is absent.
Add coverage proving `log_subdomains_off` is inherited across fork even when set before domain creation, so subdomain audit logs are correctly suppressed in children.

The group directly targets the reported bug: loss of per-credential state (`log_subdomains_off`) during fork/prepare_creds when the credential has no domain. Adding coverage for inheritance in that case matches the root cause.

candidates.rationale: This conditional wrongly prevented copying the Landlock credential state when no domain existed, which caused fields like `log_subdomains_off` to be dropped during credential transfer.
This assignment is the propagation step that should have preserved the per-credential Landlock state, but it was only executed under the faulty domain check.

vuln_statements.explanation: This conditional incorrectly gated copying of the Landlock credential blob on the presence of a domain, so domain-less credentials lost state such as log_subdomains_off during credential transfer.
This is the copy operation that should always preserve per-credential Landlock state, but it was only performed inside the faulty domain check, causing the lost state.

bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 14f6c14e9fbde4a802c10c7e770b5ba63853ebc6
Author: Mickaël Salaün <mic@digikod.net>
Date:   Thu Mar 20 20:06:57 2025 +0100

    landlock: Identify domain execution crossing
    
    Extend struct landlock_cred_security with a domain_exec bitmask to
    identify which Landlock domain were created by the current task's bprm.
    The whole bitmask is reset on each execve(2) call.
    
    Cc: Günther Noack <gnoack@google.com>
    Cc: Paul Moore <paul@paul-moore.com>
    Link: https://lore.kern
bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct is not present in this commit version. The reported bug was that the per-credential Landlock blob was only copied when `old_llcred->domain` was non-NULL, which caused state like `log_subdomains_off` to be lost on `fork()`/`prepare_creds()` for domain-less credentials. In this snippet, `hook_cred_transfer()` still checks `if (old_llcred->domain)`, but when true it now does `*landlock_cred(new) = *old_llcred;`, which copies the entire security blob rather than only the domain pointer. That directly prevents loss of other fields. The new `hook_bprm_creds_for_exec()` also resets `landlock_cred(bprm->cred)->domain_exec = 0;`, showing added handling for exec transitions. Since the bug condition described is the old partial-copy behavior, and this code already contains the corrected full-struct copy, `has_bug` is false and `is_fixed` is true.
